title: Array.from & Array.of
description: Build arrays without loops — `Array.from` with a mapper makes filled arrays; `Array.of` avoids the `new Array(n)` sparse-array trap.

notes: `Array.from({length: n})` works because length is the only property `from` needs to walk an array-like.
`new Array(3)` makes 3 EMPTY slots — `.map` skips them. `Array.from({length:3}, () => 0)` gives `[0,0,0]`.
The mapper gets `(value, index)`; for `{length}` array-likes the value is `undefined`.

questions.explain: The mapper receives `(value, index)`; index runs 0..n-1.

questions.q: Which converts a Set to an Array?
Why does `new Array(3).map(() => 0)` give `[ <3 empty> ]` instead of `[0,0,0]`?
questions.explain: Array methods like map/forEach/filter skip holes — use `Array.from({length:3}, () => 0)` instead.
